countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

courses.name: B.E./B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering
courses.summary: A four-year undergraduate engineering degree covering engineering mechanics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, machine design, manufacturing processes and control systems. Teaching is built around workshop practice, thermal and materials laboratories, computer-aided design and a final-year project. Graduates move into manufacturing, automotive, energy, thermal and design roles, or continue to a master's specialisation such as thermal engineering or machine design.

courses.name: B.E./B.Tech in Aerospace Engineering
courses.summary: The Students Traffic catalogue category for four-year undergraduate aerospace engineering degrees. Programmes in this category cover aerodynamics, flight mechanics, propulsion, aerospace structures, control systems and spacecraft dynamics, supported by wind-tunnel, propulsion and structures laboratories and a final-year design project. In India the award is a B.Tech. or B.E. over eight semesters, and international entry normally requires physics and mathematics at the school-leaving stage.

universities.name: Chandigarh University
universities.summary: Chandigarh University is a state private university established by a 2012 Act of the Punjab legislature, with its campus at Gharuan in Mohali district on the Chandigarh-Ludhiana highway. It teaches engineering, business, pharmacy, sciences, media, design, law and liberal arts in English, and admits international students through its own International Admission Department.
universities.campusLifestyle: The Gharuan campus covers more than 150 acres, and CU reports more than 2,500 international students from over 65 countries. Each academic block has its own library, and the central library opens seven days a week. Food courts sit beside every block, and two banks with four ATMs operate on campus. Classes run Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. A formal dress code applies, with student uniform on Wednesdays. The campus is alcohol-free, and CU reports smoking, drug or alcohol use to the local police.
universities.cityProfile: Gharuan is a village in Kharar tehsil of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar (Mohali) district, and the campus sits on NH-05, the Chandigarh-Ludhiana highway. Chandigarh city, railway station and international airport are the nearest hubs. From Chandigarh's ISBT Sector 43, CTU bus 20 runs to Kharar bus stand, where an auto-rickshaw covers the last stretch. Long-route buses to Ludhiana via Kharar also stop in front of the university. CU offers a free airport pickup from New Delhi or Chandigarh international airport, but only if flight details reach international@cumail.in at least two weeks before arrival. Punjab summers (May-July) run 30-44 C and winters (November-January) 2-20 C, so warm clothing is needed from November. Private rooms can be rented off campus in Kharar or Mohali.
universities.practicalExposure: The National Board of Accreditation's Tier I (Washington Accord) register lists eight B.E. programmes to 30 June 2027: Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Chemical, Computer Science and Engineering, Aerospace, Electronics and Communication, and Mechatronics. The MBA is on NBA's Management PG register to the same date. CU also runs industry-linked B.E. CSE (Hons.) tracks with IBM in AI and machine learning, cloud computing, data science, cyber security and the Internet of Things, plus a Computer Science and Business Systems track with TCS. For time abroad, CU lists a European Project Semester for engineering, management and fashion students: two months of study in Italy and four months of training with European companies. It also names semester exchanges by discipline, such as aerospace places at IPSA in France and SPbPU in Russia, and MBA exchanges in Poland, Germany, Belgium, South Korea and Taiwan. The B.A. Psychology (Hons.) includes field study, a practicum and an internship.
universities.hostelOverview: Campus hostels are single-sex, and the fee is paid yearly in advance because there is one intake. International rates per year (meals included) are: AC 5-seater, men, USD 1,950; AC 4-seater, women, USD 2,350; AC 3-seater USD 2,600; AC 2-seater, men, USD 3,140; AC single, men, USD 3,530. Non-AC rooms cost USD 2,150 for a 4-seater, USD 2,350 for a 3-seater, USD 2,750 for a 2-seater (men) and USD 3,000 for a single (men). CU says rates rise each year for the batch to cover food inflation. Rooms come with a bed, mattress, cupboard, study table and chair. Basic electricity units are free, and extra use is billed. Students who arrive without a paid booking can stay one night only.
universities.dietarySupport: Hostel messes serve Indian vegetarian meals, with non-vegetarian meals twice a week, and the cost is part of the hostel fee. SAARC students can pay a small monthly amount for upgraded meals. Students may cook in their rooms on induction heaters, paying for electricity above the free allowance. Branded and local food courts sit next to every academic block, and hostel tuck shops sell bedding and toiletries.
universities.safetyOverview: CU says the campus is guarded 24x7 with CCTV and is ragging-free, with separate emergency lines for security, medical help, the women cell and anti-ragging. A registered doctor runs OPD in working hours. Three ambulances are on campus, and medical supervisors cover the hostels 24x7. Health insurance is compulsory. Without a valid policy, about INR 3,500 a year is billed for a group cover that excludes routine OPD.
universities.studentSupport: The International Admission Department (international@cumail.in, +91 7626862200) handles admission queries. On arrival, students collect a University Identification Number and Wi-Fi access. The FRO help desk in Block A1 guides FRO registration and visa extensions, which take about 45 days. SIM cards need a passport and visa copy or the student ID card with two photographs.

faq.question: Is Chandigarh University public or private?
faq.answer: It is a state private university. It was established by the Chandigarh University Act, 2012 (Punjab Act No. 7 of 2012), which is headquartered at Gharuan in Mohali district and receives no state grant. UGC lists it among state private universities, notified on 10 July 2012, and includes it under Section 12(B) of the UGC Act following the Commission's 547th meeting in May 2020.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: CU states that English is the medium of instruction in its classes, with no switch to Hindi or Punjabi later in the degree. For international students from non-English-speaking countries, CU offers a Language Foundation Program (LFP), which can be chosen on the international registration form.

faq.question: Do international applicants need an entrance exam or an English test?
faq.answer: CU's international admission tracker has no entrance-test stage. It runs from enquiry to an eligibility check, Offer Letter, acceptance, invoice and an Acceptance Letter for the visa. CUCET belongs to CU's Indian-national route. CU's international pages publish no IELTS or TOEFL minimum, but classes are taught in English. B.Arch is different: it needs a NATA or JEE aptitude score, which is why it is not listed here.

faq.question: What are the academic entry requirements?
faq.answer: Requirements vary by programme. The B.E. CSE needs 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics plus a third science or computing subject and 60 per cent. Mechanical and Aerospace need the same subjects with 50 per cent. B.Pharm needs 60 per cent with English and PCM/PCB, AIU equivalence and a minimum age of 17. The MBA needs a bachelor's degree with 50 per cent, B.A. Psychology needs 55 per cent in any stream, and B.A. Journalism needs 50 per cent in any stream.

faq.question: How much does it cost per year in total?
faq.answer: International tuition is USD 3,200 per semester for the listed B.E. branches (USD 6,400 a year), USD 3,700 per semester for the MBA and B.Pharm, USD 2,200 for M.Sc. Chemistry and USD 1,900 for the B.A. programmes. Hostels with meals add USD 1,950-3,530 a year depending on the room. Insurance adds about INR 3,500 a year unless you hold a valid policy, plus charges such as uniform and fest fees. SAARC nationals pay separate rupee rates.

faq.question: Are scholarships available for international students?
faq.answer: CU advertises a merit scholarship of up to 50 per cent for international students, but it does not publish the marks bands or which fee components it covers. Government of India scholarships run separately through the ICCR. Students Traffic can help you request the scholarship terms in writing before you pay the first-semester fee.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Register on CU's international portal at cuchd.in/international/registration and upload your Grade 10 and Grade 12 (or degree) results, translated into English where needed, with a grade-percentage equivalency certificate. After the eligibility check, CU issues an Offer Letter. You then sign the Acceptance of Offer Letter, pay the invoiced fee by SWIFT, and receive the Acceptance Letter used for the student visa.

faq.question: When is the intake and when should I apply?
faq.answer: CU has one academic intake a year. Its calendar sets the start of the AY 2027-28 session for 14 July 2027. No fixed international closing date is published, but the first semester fee must be paid on or before arrival. Late reporting counts against attendance, and CU asks late arrivals to seek written permission from international@cumail.in. Allow up to three months for the visa.

faq.question: What visa and FRRO steps apply after admission?
faq.answer: Apply for an Indian student visa endorsed in the name of Chandigarh University, Mohali, using CU's Acceptance Letter; Nepalese and Bhutanese nationals are exempt. The Bureau of Immigration requires FRRO/FRO registration within 14 days of arrival for visas longer than 180 days and prohibits work and business on a student visa. CU's FRO help desk in Block A1 handles registration and extensions.

faq.question: What is Chandigarh University's accreditation status?
faq.answer: NAAC accredited CU A+ with a CGPA of 3.28 in Cycle 1, declared in September 2019, and it remains on NAAC's list of institutions with valid accreditation. No newer cycle has been declared through December 2025. NBA's Tier I (Washington Accord) register lists eight B.E. branches, and its Management PG register lists the MBA, all to 30 June 2027. NIRF 2025 ranks CU 19th among universities.

faq.question: What accommodation is available and what does it cost?
faq.answer: Campus hostels are single-sex and are paid yearly in advance, with meals included. International rates run from USD 1,950 for an AC 5-seater (men) and USD 2,150 for a non-AC 4-seater to USD 3,530 for an AC single (men). Women's rooms are the AC 4-seater at USD 2,350 and the shared 3-seater categories. CU says rates rise each year to cover food inflation, and private rooms are available in Kharar and Mohali.

faq.question: Can I change programme after arriving?
faq.answer: Yes. CU allows a programme change after arrival, before a deadline it announces, if seats are available, and a nominal administrative fee may apply. Transcripts still pending at admission must be submitted within one week of reporting, or within a week of the result being published if it was awaited.

faq.question: How does CU compare with other private universities in Punjab?
faq.answer: In NIRF 2025, CU ranks 19th in the University category and 31st in Engineering. Its B.E. international tuition is USD 3,200 per semester, and SAARC nationals pay a separate rupee tier. Its NAAC grade dates from a 2019 Cycle 1 declaration, so compare declaration years as well as grades when you shortlist Punjab universities.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.
